question: Researchers from which institute built a portable desalination unit that generates clear, clean drinking water without the need for filters or high-pressure pumps in April 2022?

options.text: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Hong Kong

solution:
The correct answer is __**Massachusetts Institute of Technology, USA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Researchers from the **Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), USA**, developed a portable desalination unit in April 2022.
 
• The device is capable of generating clear and clean drinking water without the need for traditional filters or high-pressure pumps.
 
• This portable desalination unit utilizes a technique called **ion concentration polarization (ICP)** to remove salts and impurities from seawater.
 
• The unit is lightweight and compact, weighing less than 10 kilograms, making it suitable for use in remote or disaster-struck areas.
 
• The device is designed to be energy-efficient, requiring only a small amount of power, which can be supplied through a portable solar panel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ion Concentration Polarization (ICP):**

 
 
• ICP is a desalination technique that uses an electric field to separate charged particles, such as salts, from water.
 
• Unlike traditional reverse osmosis, ICP does not rely on physical filters, reducing maintenance requirements.
 
 
 
• **Reverse Osmosis vs. ICP:**
 
 
• Reverse osmosis uses high-pressure pumps to force water through a semipermeable membrane, removing impurities.
 
• ICP, on the other hand, is a low-pressure method that consumes less energy and avoids clogging issues.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Portable Desalination Units:**
 
 
• These devices are valuable in disaster response scenarios where access to clean drinking water is limited.
 
• They can also be used in remote areas, military operations, and during outdoor expeditions.
 
 
 
• **Global Water Scarcity:**
 
 
• According to the United Nations, around 2.2 billion people globally lack access to safe drinking water.
 
• Innovations like portable desalination units can help alleviate water scarcity in affected regions.
